I find the components with the second derivative, separate them with a Gaussian fit and assign them: β-sheet 1615–1637, disordered 1637–1645, α-helix 1645–1662, turn 1662–1681, antiparallel β/aggregates 1681–1700 cm⁻¹ (Byler & Susi 1986; Barth 2007). Useful for proteins, wool, silk, collagen and protein binders. In aqueous solution the water (1640 cm⁻¹) must be subtracted first; the boundaries between classes are indicative.

Un modo per avere percentuali in peso an: A way to get weight percentages even without standards: from physical laws (how many X-rays the tube emits, how many each element absorbs, how many it re-emits) I calculate the signal that a given composition would produce, and I change the composition until the calculation matches the spectrum. It is intended for alloys and compact materials, but it is a calculation with assumptions: verified on simulated spectra, not yet on certified materials. With a similar standard it becomes much more precise; results should always be presented as estimates.

XRF composition was calculated by the fu: XRF composition was calculated by the fundamental-parameters method: primary intensities for a thick homogeneous sample according to Sherman (1955) and secondary fluorescence according to Shiraiwa & Fujino (1966), with cross sections, edge energies and fluorescence yields from xraylib (Schoonjans et al., 2011); the tube spectrum was modelled as a Kramers continuum with anode self-absorption plus characteristic lines (simplified form of Ebel, 1999), with beryllium windows, air path and silicon-detector efficiency. Line areas were obtained by fitting all K, L and M lines of each element (Gaussians with the detector resolution, silicon escape peaks, Rayleigh and Compton scattered tube lines, B-spline background) by weighted non-negative least squares (Lawson & Hanson, 1974), iterating the line ratios predicted for the matrix. Concentrations were normalised to 100% (alloys), as oxides (glass and ceramics), or scaled to the Compton peak with an assumed invisible matrix (paint layers); where stated, the sensitivity of each element was calibrated on standards of known composition. The tube spectrum and fluorescence yields are approximated; without standards the values are semi-quantitative estimates, checked on simulated spectra and not on certified materials.
